item.title: From raw interaction to reusable knowledge: Rethinking memory for AI agents
item.description:
Author: Ke Yang, Michel Galley, Chenglong Wang, Jianfeng Gao, Jiawei Han, ChengXiang Zhai
Date: March 10, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Machine Learning", "Knowledge Management", "AI Agents"]
Summary:
  • AI agents often struggle with large, unorganized interaction histories.
  • Excessive raw memory can overwhelm agents with irrelevant context.
  • PlugMem transforms these logs into structured, reusable knowledge units.
  • It focuses on storing propositional facts and prescriptive skills.
  • This approach reduces redundancy and improves retrieval precision.
  • The system enhances performance while using fewer memory tokens.

item.title: ML Safety Newsletter #14
item.description:
Author: Alice Blair
Date: (Publication date unknown)
Tags: ["AI Safety", "Cybersecurity", "Machine Learning", "Prompt Engineering"]
Summary:
  • Google DeepMind researchers developed CaMeL to stop prompt injection attacks.
  • These attacks trick AI agents into following malicious external instructions.
  • CaMeL forces the AI to commit to a specific plan in advance.
